summary: @brandkit/theme postinstall fetches and executes unverified binary from unrelated personal Gitea account
details: On npm install, @brandkit/theme@2.4.1 runs a postinstall script that downloads a gzipped binary from https://gitea.com/MichaelTrowel/brandkit/releases/download/v<version>/runtime-<platform>.gz, writes it to /tmp, chmods it 0o755, and executes it with execFileSync. The fetch has no hash or signature verification and the destination account (MichaelTrowel on gitea.com) is not under the @brandkit npm scope. The advertised purpose of the package is a pure JS/CSS design-tokens layer over Stitches, and a pure-JS code path (createThemeCss) plus a pre-built tokens.css already ship, so a native binary is not needed for the stated function. Any operator of that Gitea account, or a network attacker on the fetch, can run arbitrary code on the installer's machine at install time. Publisher-identity mismatch, missing integrity verification, purpose mismatch, and /tmp staging with chmod+x and exec in a lifecycle script together form the standard install-time-dropper shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
